title: A point unramified in a locally finite type morphism is isolated in its fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and write $\kappa(s)$ for the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Assume that $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and unramified at $x$ in the sense of [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then the point of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ corresponding to $x$ is open (and hence isolated) in $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Equivalently, the singleton $\{x\}$ is open in the underlying topological fibre. (Stacks Project, Tags [02GF] and [02G8], with local quasi-finiteness from Tag [02V5].)
